hero.headline: Four arrested in Martin County after armed robbery of teen and police pursuit
hero.body:
Four suspects were arrested in Martin County on Monday following an armed robbery of a teenager and a subsequent police pursuit, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. The arrests concluded a chase that ended with deputies taking all four individuals into custody.

The incident began with the armed robbery of a teenage victim. Deputies responded and pursued the suspects through Martin County. The pursuit ended with the apprehension of all four accused individuals.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office handled the investigation and arrests. The suspects face charges related to the armed robbery and the pursuit that followed.

Deputies confirmed the arrests were made Monday. The teenage victim was targeted in the armed robbery that led to the law enforcement response and chase through the county.

cards.headline: Trump intervened with FIFA president before Balogun red card suspension lifted for World Cup match
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump called FIFA president Gianni Infantino to ask for a review of the red card that suspended U.S. forward Folarin Balogun, according to a person familiar with the call.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump intervened on behalf of American forward Folarin Balogun, whose red-card suspension was lifted in a decision that allows him to play in Monday's World Cup round of 16 match against Belgium in Seattle. Trump called FIFA president Gianni Infantino after Wednesday's round of 32 game asking FIFA to review the red card, according to a person familiar with the call who spoke on condition of anonymity because the person was not authorized to speak publicly about the matter. FIFA announced Sunday that Balogun's one-game suspension had been lifted. The decision appeared to be the first time since 1962 that a red card during a World Cup did not result in a suspension. Trump posted on social media thanking FIFA for doing what was right and reversing a great injustice.

Balogun received a red card for stepping awkwardly on the right ankle of Bosnia-Herzegovina's Tarik Muharemović during a 2-0 United States victory on Wednesday. Brazilian referee Raphael Claus didn't initially signal a card but showed Balogun red after a video review. The Royal Belgian Football Association said it was astonished and stated it is investigating all potential options to safeguard the legitimate rights of participating teams and protect fair play principles. Belgium coach Rudi Garcia said through a translator that he didn't know that in FIFA offices the fifth of July was the first of April in Europe, making an April Fools' Day comparison. American players learned of Balogun's availability when social media posts appeared during their Sunday morning bus ride to training at the University of Washington's Husky Soccer Stadium. The 25-year-old Monaco forward has scored three goals in the tournament, matching Landon Donovan in 2010 for second-most by an American in a World Cup behind Bert Patenaude's four goals in 1930.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds skips Florida GOP governor debate as rivals mention him 60 times
cards.teaser: U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds, the Trump-backed frontrunner for Florida governor, dominated Thursday night's Republican debate without attending. Former House Speaker Paul Renner, Lt. Jay Collins, and businessman James Fishback mentioned Donalds by name at least 60 times during the two-hour event.
cards.body:
Byron Donalds skipped Florida's first major Republican gubernatorial debate Thursday night, but the Trump-backed frontrunner still dominated the two-hour event. The three candidates who did show up, former House Speaker Paul Renner, Lt. Gov. Jeanette Nuñez, and businessman James Fishback, mentioned Donalds by name at least 60 times as each tried to position himself as the strongest alternative to the congressman.

Moderator Patrick Bet-David called Donalds "the elephant not in the room" and said he had urged the congressman to attend. Bet-David said Donalds told him he has raised roughly $100 million, is polling between 48 percent and 58 percent, and would only consider debating once another candidate hits double digits. "Till then, I'm not showing up," Bet-David said, summarizing Donalds' response. Collins criticized Donalds for refusing to debate, saying "We don't do kings in the United States of America. We sure don't do them in Florida." He added that if Donalds wants the governor's mansion, "you've got to grow a spine, you've got to stand up, and you've got to fight for the people of Florida." Renner called Donalds' absence disrespectful and said "Every voter in this audience, everyone watching, everyone in the state deserves a debate." Fishback contrasted Donalds' fundraising with his own ground game, noting his campaign was the first in Florida running for governor to visit all 67 counties.

The debate centered on affordability, property taxes, insurance, and hyperscale data centers. Fishback went furthest on taxes, saying "I don't support relieving your property taxes. I don't support reforming your property taxes. I support one thing, and one thing only, and that is completely and totally abolishing property taxes in the state of Florida." He promised to take a "chainsaw" to local government spending. Renner pitched his "Florida First" plan to eliminate most homestead property taxes while shifting more burden to tourists, out-of-state investors, and large corporations. The sharpest clash came over data centers, with Fishback promising to "reject and remove every experimental data center" in Florida and Renner saying he would call a special session to stop hyperscale projects.

The debate gave Renner, Collins, and Fishback clips and contrasts to pressure Donalds over skipping the stage. But with Donalds still holding the polling, fundraising, and endorsement advantages, one debate without him is unlikely to reset the race on its own. The anti-Donalds lane remains split among three candidates, each trying to prove which one deserves a one-on-one fight with the frontrunner.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation in Fort Pierce attracts global artists to historic Crain Estate
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain who once called the property home.
cards.body:
The nonprofit organization is tucked away in the historic Crain Estate, which was a private residence owned by Jaxson and Mary Crain. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility, from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday and Friday. The house includes a smoking and bourbon room with man paneling, a bathroom in manly colors, pre-stained glass, and a bar on the front of the patio. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India that features tiny peacocks. The estate remains 90 percent the way it was when the Crains were there.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, originally bringing in seven birds that have multiplied to over 100. One beloved bird named Bob is believed to be 60 years old and walks with a limp. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world, offering simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, with the majority being one-on-one classes where people with zero experience walk out with a piece of art. Masters said art is a form of therapy that distresses people who leave happy and have not been on their phone scrolling.

cards.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach in November
cards.body:
Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. announced the 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach this November. The festival has become an annual tradition for Indian River County residents and visitors seeking fresh seafood and coastal entertainment.

The event will take place in Vero Beach, continuing its long-running tradition as one of the Treasure Coast's signature food festivals. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. organizes the annual gathering, which draws attendees from across the region.

The festival typically features fresh seafood from local and regional vendors, along with live entertainment and family activities. Vero Beach has hosted the event for nearly two decades, making it a staple in the community's calendar of annual events.

Specific dates and venue details for the November festival will be announced by Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. The event attracts thousands of visitors each year to Indian River County, supporting local tourism and the regional seafood industry.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, putting the Peacock Arts District on the map. The nonprofit preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain in the historic Crain Estate.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation operates from the historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain who once called the property home. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling, according to art director Krystal Masters. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India that features tiny peacocks on it. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday and Friday. The estate remains 90 percent the way it was when the Crains lived there, including the smoking and bourbon room with its man paneling, manly colored bathroom, pre-stained glass, and a bar on the front patio.

The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, bringing in seven originally that have grown to over 100 birds. Among the flock is a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old and the oldest peacock on the property, who walks with a limp and is hand-fed daily from his own bowls. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world with simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, and visitors do not need professional experience to participate. Masters leads one-on-one classes where students with zero experience walk out with a piece of art.

hero.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
hero.body:
A 40-year-old man was killed early Sunday after a head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened around 2 a.m. near State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane.

FHP said a 2015 Kia Optima was traveling north on State Road 710 when the driver crossed into the southbound lane and collided head-on with a 2021 Toyota Tundra. The front left of the Kia struck the front left of the Tundra. Upon impact, the Kia burst into flames and came to rest on the grass shoulder facing north. The Tundra came to rest facing southeast in the southbound lane. The driver of the Kia, a 40-year-old man, died at the scene. The driver of the Tundra, a 41-year-old man from Indiantown, was taken to the hospital via LifeStar medical helicopter.

Martin County Fire Rescue has responded to 42 vehicle accident-related calls on State Road 710 just this year. After a fatal crash in January, Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek called the road a death trap. Bill Townsend, who lives nearby, said the road has long been a concern for residents. "People don't pay a whole lot of attention to other people on the road, and kind of a dangerous road sometimes," Townsend said. "Everybody's always in a hurry. Just living here makes me worry about the young people learning to drive and learning to drive on that road concerns me, because I have young kids."

The Florida Department of Transportation has plans to widen the road from two lanes to four but construction is not expected to begin until 2031. "The question will be how many more people have to die before we get that project going. Florida touts that they have the safest roads in the country but this road is one that clearly is not in that category," Budensiek said in January. In the meantime, FDOT has begun improvements to the road, including pavement, markings, signage and new turn lanes. Townsend said faster action is needed. "It would be beneficial to the people that live and travel that road all the time if something happened faster," Townsend said.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie approves land transfer for new Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with the interchange. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie and the interchange is about accessibility and keeping up with growth.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase and construction is anticipated to begin in Summer 2027.

The partial interchange for the Turnpike is still in the design phase. Erin Scheumeister, a Port St. Lucie resident, said the construction can be annoying but she believes it is necessary and it will be a lot better and easier to get to work. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiance Misty Dawn White in deadly house fire
cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiance in a deadly home fire earlier this week.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help White's fiancé Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, said she received a call from Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire. Fenn returned to the scene in the days following the tragedy to process her grief and described the situation as completely a state of devastation. Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured after losing his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. Fenn said Misty was a Christian woman who loved gardening and plants, plays the piano, loves kids and was always the first to lend a hand. White's birthday is the Fourth of July, so she passed just a few days before her birthday. Fenn said White has always been a good soul and will always be in their hearts.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit rescues 2 after boat sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from marine deputies and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. The sheriff's office said in a Facebook post that this incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life. The sheriff's office added that they are grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by their Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes today for $3 million renovation to nearly double slip capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock closes July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity from 18 to 44 slips for motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees and will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually. Boat captain Parker Fisher said the dock has needed work over the years and he is glad they are putting money into it, expressing hope for more floating docks to be added.

During the closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, initially had concerns about continuing to run during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city is allowing them to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock's non-floating section so they can board people at that location. Kuyrkendall said Stuart is not Stuart without the water and noted the dock can get hectic on weekends when his operation squeezes in and tries to find spots. He said modernizing and expanding the dock is really going to be great for the city and for his business.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with sister Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: Serena Williams pulled out of her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday, citing a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury. The 44-year-old Serena was injured during her singles return earlier in the week in a three-set loss. She announced the withdrawal in an Instagram post, writing that she did everything she could but her knee was not ready to compete. The post included images of four syringes showing fluid that was drained from her knee after her singles match. An accompanying video showed her walking with strapping up and down her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her. Serena was beaten 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 by 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday.

The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in the only first-round doubles match that was not scheduled earlier in the week, having been pushed back to give Serena more time to recover. Venus, who is 46, played in the mixed doubles tournament on Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena indicated she could play again somewhere else soon, telling followers to stay tuned to a city near you. The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon.

cards.headline: Argentina survives Cape Verde scare 3-2 in World Cup thriller
cards.teaser: Defending World Cup champion Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 in extra time Friday, with Lionel Messi scoring his 20th career World Cup goal before the match went to the wire in South Florida.
cards.body:
Argentina advanced to the World Cup Round of 16 after defeating Cape Verde 3-2 in a match that required extra time to decide. The go-ahead score came in the 111th minute when Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges for an own goal. Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1.

Lionel Messi scored in the 29th minute, taking a quick touch on a lofted pass from Martinez and hammering a finish into the roof of the net past goalkeeper Vozinha for a 1-0 lead. The goal was Messi's 20th career World Cup goal, extending his record, and his seventh goal of this tournament. He has 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak, moving two goals ahead of France's Kylian Mbappé on the all-time World Cup list.

Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored equalizers for Cape Verde that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida. Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, 40, made 10 saves including five against Messi. Argentina will face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday after Egypt beat Australia in a penalty shootout earlier Friday.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots finished last season with a 10-2 record and a district title, but a second-round playoff exit left the team wanting more as they prepare for the 2026 fall football season. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the seniors are four-year players, with the majority coming from the middle school program. Robertson said the players know how things are run and have had success in their careers, expressing hope that their senior year will be the best season the program has had.

The program is leaning into a more demanding schedule this fall. Senior Jack Williams said the team wanted to take the program to the next level by playing against really good teams to compete and attract new people. Senior Jack Whelche said a better year means going farther in the playoffs. He said the team wants to go undefeated in the season, but that does not matter if they keep losing in the second round of the playoffs. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily summer workouts add up as something to look forward to, noting the team is working harder to see positive results when the season comes and break their record.

The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach in November
hero.body:
Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. announced the 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach this November. The festival has become an annual tradition for Indian River County residents and visitors seeking fresh seafood and coastal entertainment.

The event will take place in Vero Beach, continuing its long-running tradition as one of the Treasure Coast's signature food festivals. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. organizes the annual gathering, which draws attendees from across the region.

The festival typically features fresh seafood from local and regional vendors, along with live entertainment and family activities. Vero Beach has hosted the event for nearly two decades, making it a staple in the community's calendar of annual events.

Specific dates and venue details for the November festival will be announced by Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. The event attracts thousands of visitors each year to Indian River County, supporting local tourism and the regional seafood industry.

hero.headline: Four arrested in Martin County after armed robbery of teen and police pursuit
hero.body:
Four suspects were arrested in Martin County on Monday following an armed robbery of a teenager and a subsequent police pursuit, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. The arrests concluded a chase that ended with deputies taking all four individuals into custody.

The incident began with the armed robbery of a teenage victim. Deputies responded and pursued the suspects through Martin County. The pursuit ended with the apprehension of all four accused individuals.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office handled the investigation and arrests. The suspects face charges related to the armed robbery and the pursuit that followed.

Deputies confirmed the arrests were made Monday. The teenage victim was targeted in the armed robbery that led to the law enforcement response and chase through the county.
